solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mortgagor ill-advised to accommodate thug

indicators.note: the words Mortgagor ill-advised are said to accommodate, or hold within them, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A borrower is warned against taking in some heavy who needs a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' marks the answer as sitting inside 'mortGAGOR ILL-Advised', running across the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is informal for a big, brutish heavy employed for muscle, a thug.

clue.text: Government department once implicated in blunder is one of high standing

indicators.note: the department is implicated in, caught inside, the blunder

parts.note: a gaffe is a blunder
IR, the Inland Revenue, was a former UK government department

explanation.surface: A former ministry is caught up in a scandal involving a top official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of high standing' sounds like a dignitary; it is the tallest animal, which stands high. The Inland Revenue merged into HMRC in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe is literally tall standing, the tallest living land animal.

clue.text: Artist must change image to accommodate mass market in the end

indicators.note: the change-image word is to accommodate, take in, the mass

parts.note: to rebrand is to change one's image
M is the symbol for mass in physics

indicators.note: in the end means market's final letter

explanation.surface: A painter has to reinvent himself to reach popular buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was the great Dutch painter, an artist by example.

clue.text: Drink flat white after sustaining losses on both fronts

indicators.note: each of the two words, flat and white, suffers losses at its front, its opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone orders a flat white after hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAT loses F, WHITE loses WHI, leaving LAT and TE; unevenly, as solvers noted. A flat white is a similar coffee, misleading as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a milky espresso coffee, one kind of drink.

clue.text: First model to bend over backwards on top of classic Jag

indicators.note: in a down answer, the bending word sits on top of the car

parts.note: to arch is to bend the body over backwards
the E-Type is the classic 1960s Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A model contorts herself over the bonnet of a vintage Jaguar.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern or prototype from which copies are made.

clue.text: Manuscript account taken from pope's office by Russia

indicators.note: account is to be taken out of the word for the pope's office, removing those letters

parts.note: the papacy is the office of the pope
RUS is the international vehicle code for Russia

explanation.surface: Records of a financial transaction are removed from the Vatican by Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' leaves PAPY; 'Manuscript' is fair because papyrus also means a document written on that material.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus can mean an ancient document written on that reed paper, i.e. a manuscript.

clue.text: One refuses to be seen in tartan without naked sex appeal

indicators.note: without here means outside: the trimmed tartan goes around the other piece
one refuses to be seen in the tartan word, so it is removed

parts.note: plaid is tartan cloth
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone won't appear in tartan lacking any bare sexiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'naked' sex leaves E.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest request, to appeal.

clue.text: 90% appreciate being represented by heads

indicators.note: being represented means the letters are presented again in a new order

parts.note: taking 90% of the ten-letter word means its final tenth, the last letter, is left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Nine-tenths of people value being given a voice.
explanation.walkthrough: '90%' keeps nine of the ten letters of 'appreciate', dropping an E; 'being represented' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for 'by heads', meaning for each person.

clue.text: New ruse in Scrabble? Marked tiles!

indicators.note: to scrabble is to scramble about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sneaky new tactic in the board game with lettered tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' looks like the game; it signals scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are ancient alphabet characters, often carved on stones or tiles for divination.

clue.text: Vessel needs time in deep water, both home and abroad

indicators.note: time goes in, inside, the first sea word

parts.note: the sea is deep water
mer is the French for sea, deep water abroad

explanation.surface: A ship has to spend time at sea, in home waters and overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep water' is used twice: SEA at home and MER, its French word, abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship, a vessel driven by steam power.

clue.text: Give up on university

parts.note: RE means on, concerning, as in a letter heading
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a university

explanation.surface: An order to abandon one's university studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to relinquish or cancel, for instance a debt or penalty, so to give it up.

clue.text: Go-ahead king seduced by risk, losing last of wealth

indicators.note: the king is seduced, drawn in and held, by the risk word, so he goes inside it
the risk word loses a letter, which is then taken out

parts.note: a chance is a risk

indicators.note: the last of wealth means its final letter

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A monarch lured by danger gives permission, though his fortune slips away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops H ('last of wealth') to leave CANCE, which 'seduced by' wraps around the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission to proceed, synonymous with a go-ahead.

clue.text: Journo goes after church involved in misguided offer to indoctrinate

indicators.note: the journalist goes after, i.e. follows, the rest in the answer
church is involved in, set inside, the rearranged letters of offer
a misguided offer is one gone astray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ED, short for editor, is the usual journalist in crosswords

explanation.surface: A reporter follows a churchman caught up in a badly judged offer to brainwash someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' reworks the letters into FORFE; 'involved in' sets the church inside, giving FORCEFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To force-feed ideas is to cram them into someone without choice, the figurative sense of indoctrinating.

clue.text: Tea service returned following introduction of annulment

indicators.note: the service word comes following that letter in the answer
the introduction of annulment is its opening letter
returned means the service word is read backwards

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Tea is sent back after the start of a marriage annulment, as if a wedding reception went sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives SSAM, which comes 'following' the first letter of annulment.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea grown in that north-east Indian state.

clue.text: Tedium induced, essentially, through unlimited court action?

indicators.note: the middle letter goes through, inside, the trimmed court game
unlimited means the court game loses its limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: tennis is action on a court, not in a law court

indicators.note: essentially means the heart, the central letter, of induced

explanation.surface: Boredom brought on by endless litigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court action' looks legal but is TENNIS; 'unlimited' trims it to ENNI and U (centre of 'induced', 'essentially') goes 'through' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for listless weariness, the same as tedium.

clue.text: Jew from Eilat is disgruntled with religious education

indicators.note: disgruntled suggests upset or disturbed, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Someone from the Israeli resort of Eilat is unhappy with their schooling in faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the ancient Hebrew nation, hence a Jew.

clue.text: Rumpy-pumpy with poor Kiki moving twice this fast

indicators.note: the letters are moved about to make the answer twice over, so one copy is left after the first

parts.note: this refers to the answer itself, the second copy the letters make

explanation.surface: Bawdy goings-on with a hapless Kiki, set beside the solemnity of a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The eighteen letters of RUMPYPUMPY, POOR and KIKI rearrange into the answer twice; 'moving twice this' says so.
explanation.definitionFit: Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, is the holiest Jewish day, observed by fasting.

clue.text: Way to transport Manx politician around?

definitions.text: Way to transport Manx politician around?

indicators.note: the way word carries the others within it, as if transporting them

parts.note: a mode is a way

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the politician loses his last letter

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative politician
CA, circa, means around

explanation.surface: How should a politician from the Isle of Man be carted about?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' means tailless, from the tailless Manx cat, so TORY becomes TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a procession of cars that carries a dignitary such as a politician.

clue.text: Spurious name setter's rejected for sobriquet

parts.note: pseudo means false, spurious

indicators.note: rejected means the setter's name is turned back

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so setter's is MY

explanation.surface: A false name is turned down as a nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name setter's' means the setter's name, MY N, reversed to NYM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is an assumed name, loosely a nickname or sobriquet.

clue.text: Cut off fungal growth in between toes (at the top)

indicators.note: the fungus sits in, inside, the between word followed by the letter

parts.note: inter- is the prefix meaning between

indicators.note: at the top of toes means its first letter

parts.note: a cep is a large edible mushroom, a fungal growth

explanation.surface: Something fungal sprouting between the toes, like athlete's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: CEP goes 'in' INTER plus T ('toes' 'at the top').
explanation.definitionFit: To intercept is to stop and seize something in transit, cutting it off.

clue.text: Outside term-time, university is granted nothing without specific application

parts.note: in the vac, the vacation, is outside term-time
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A university is given nothing in the holidays without applying for it.
explanation.definitionFit: In vacuo, Latin for 'in a vacuum', means considered in isolation, without reference to context.

clue.text: Ground hosting final of competition?

indicators.note: the ground word is hosting, holding within it, the final letter

parts.note: an area is a piece of ground

indicators.note: the final of competition is its last letter

explanation.surface: A stadium is chosen to stage a cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: N ('final of competition') inside AREA; and an arena does host finals, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a stadium or enclosed ground where contests such as finals are staged.

clue.text: Free from contamination after a month in charge

indicators.note: the in-charge abbreviation comes after the month

parts.note: Sept is short for September

explanation.surface: Cleansed after a month in charge of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means sterile, free of germs and contamination.

clue.text: Worth having sides of uniform straightened for regulator

indicators.note: uniform is U in the phonetic alphabet; straighten that letter's curved sides and it becomes another letter

parts.note: value means worth

explanation.surface: A garment's edges are pressed flat to improve it.
explanation.walkthrough: The U of VALUE, its rounded sides drawn straight, becomes a V.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve is a device that controls the flow of fluid, so it acts as a regulator.

clue.text: Fun to be had, as poet's not at home

indicators.note: IN means at home, so not at home removes those letters

parts.note: Philip Larkin was an English poet; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Good times are to be had because the poet is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks are pranks or bits of fun, as in 'for a lark'.

clue.text: Servant secures right to free gift from Carol

indicators.note: the servant secures, holds inside, the other pieces

parts.note: a page is a young servant
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: An attendant obtains the entitlement to release a present from someone called Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is the Christmas carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, whose first gift is a partridge in a pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In that song 'my true love gave to me a partridge in a pear tree', a gift in the carol.

clue.text: Test for the value of banks? On the contrary

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: banks are the edges, so the outer letters of value
on the contrary turns the phrase round, so it is the banks of the value, not the value of banks

explanation.surface: An assay of how much banks are worth, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the value of banks' the other way about: the banks of 'value', VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove something is to test it, as in proving dough or the proof of the pudding.

clue.text: Papers providing support for doctor's firm

indicators.note: in a down answer, the papers sit beneath and so support the doctor word

parts.note: to doctor is to rig or falsify; the 's is 'is', linking to the definition
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Documents backing a medic's surgery are solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and unbending, so firm.

clue.text: Order troops to disrupt most of festival

indicators.note: the troops go in to disrupt, breaking into, the shortened festival
most of the festival word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: a carnival is a festival
OR, other ranks, are troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers are commanded to break up a street party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command but is the biological rank; 'most of' leaves CARNIVA for the troops to break into.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnivora is the mammalian order of meat-eaters such as cats, dogs and bears.

clue.text: I'm like a cat, say, knocking back fish

indicators.note: knocking back means the word for say is turned back to front

parts.note: EG, for example, means say
to net is to catch, to fish

explanation.surface: A cat-like creature boasts of downing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the animal speaks of itself. EG 'knocking back' gives GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The genet is a slender spotted carnivore resembling a cat, related to civets.

clue.text: Indecent part of former pupil's act?

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school; the 's joins the pieces
a scene is part of an act in a play, which the words part of point to

explanation.surface: A school leaver's stage turn proves rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene describes something offensive to standards of decency, so indecent.

clue.text: Destroy rodents circulating disease

parts.note: to end something is to destroy it

indicators.note: circulating moves a letter of the rodents round from the back to the front

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: Killing rats and mice stops illness spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' sends the final letter round to the front, giving EMIC; endemic is used here as a noun, an endemic disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic is a disease regularly found in a particular area or population.
